record.paper_title: On some open problems of number theory
record.original_question: A positive integer is perfect when it is equal to the sum of all of its proper divisors. Is there any odd perfect number?

artifact.self_contained_problem: For a positive integer $n$, let $\sigma(n)$ denote the sum of all positive divisors of $n$. A positive integer $n$ is called perfect if it equals the sum of its proper positive divisors, equivalently if $\sigma(n) = 2n$. Determine whether there exists an odd perfect number, i.e., an odd positive integer $n$ such that $\sigma(n) = 2n$.
artifact.status_search_result: The existence of an odd perfect number is a famous long-standing open problem in number theory. No odd perfect number has ever been found, and known lower bounds (e.g., any odd perfect number must exceed $10^{1500}$, with various restrictions on the number of distinct prime factors and prime structure) continue to be improved, but the problem remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Perfect number - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: It is not known whether any odd perfect numbers exist; various results have been obtained, but none has led to a proof of existence or non-existence.
status_evidence.claim: The existence of an odd perfect number is open.

status_evidence.title: Odd perfect numbers - Ochem & Rao
status_evidence.snippet: Lower bounds and constraints on odd perfect numbers are continually improved, but existence remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Active research on bounds, but problem unresolved.
